item.title: Surel's Place: Month-Long Artist Residency (September 2026 deadline)
item.description:
Organisation: Surel's Place

Location: In person in Garden City, Idaho, USA (Boise area). Residents must live at the home and studio; no studio-only residencies.

Award: Free rent, utilities and wi-fi, a living stipend of USD 100 per week, a USD 300 travel stipend, use of well-maintained bicycles, free or discounted tickets to art events and movies, marketing through Surel's Place channels, and event hosting including logistics and installation help. Each resident also gets a local host to orient them and host their public events. No application fee. NOTE: Surel's Place takes a commission on sales arising from the residency, 35% of retail price on artwork, 45% on ticketed events that are offsite or need contracted services (calculated after administrative expenses), and 15% on books, CDs or other merchandise tangential to the artist's medium. A surcharge may apply to cover additional utility costs if a partner joins.

Duration: One month (longer may be possible if justified in the application). The 1 September deadline covers residencies in January to May of the following year, beginning four months after the deadline; the 1 March deadline covers July to November of the same year.

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

Surel's Place is a residency in Garden City, Idaho with a two-fold mission: to give artists the time, shelter and professional support their work deserves, and to give the public accessible art experiences including performances, readings, exhibits and workshops. In exchange for the residency, artists offer art experiences back to the community. OPEN TO professional visual, literary and performance artists: painters, writers, musicians, architects, filmmakers, choreographers, any artist who needs a place to focus. LIMITS: because of the property's constraints and proximity to neighbours, it cannot accommodate loud or very messy processes such as welding or blacksmithing. The organisers also note that predominantly conceptual work, work that must be explained to attract a viewer, may not be met with as much enthusiasm by the jurors, and that they welcome artists who want to connect with an audience. Each cycle, one of the five residencies includes outreach to local schools through the PARTNER Schools Program. REQUIREMENTS: maintain residence at the home and studio (no studio-use-only residencies); use the residency in a focused way towards a stated goal with no other employment or work happening simultaneously; visual artists give a show of and/or lecture about their residency work, writers give a reading and discussion session; all artists offer at least one public workshop (2 to 3 hours, minimal lecturing); visual artists donate one piece of art to Surel's Place for future fundraising; writers allow Surel's Place to publish a free-standing excerpt of their residency work in books, broadsides, posters or similar. SALES COMMISSION applies as set out in the funding notes. HOUSE RULES: the non-smoking requirement is non-negotiable and any evidence of smoking is grounds for early termination. Partners are welcome but children and pets cannot be accommodated, no more than two adults may live there during a residency, and partners wanting concurrent residencies must apply and be accepted separately. ELIGIBILITY: applicants must be 25 or older and non-smokers. APPLY by email to info@surelsplace.org with the online Artist in Residence application plus, for VISUAL ARTISTS, a cover letter introducing yourself and saying why you want to be at Surel's Place specifically, a proposal including a workshop outline, a CV, electronic images of 4 to 6 pieces of work and an image list (title, size, medium, year); for LITERARY applicants, cover letter, proposal with workshop outline, CV and PDF work samples with your name and page number in the top right corner (fiction, prose or script no more than 10 typed double-spaced pages; poetry no more than six poems and no more than 10 pages); for OTHER MEDIUMS, cover letter, proposal with workshop outline, CV and electronic samples (contact Surel's Place to discuss sample requirements for your medium). Applications are reviewed by juries of accomplished artists, writers and fine arts professionals, and all applicants are notified by email.

item.title: LATITUDE Artist in Residence 2027 (Chicago)
item.description:
Organisation: LATITUDE Chicago

Location: Chicago, Illinois, USA. No housing stipend offered.

Award: One-month production residency for 8-10 artists: a $1,000 printing stipend, unlimited scanning, a personal studio with a calibrated workstation, staff training and guidance on tech, an organised public event, and lifetime free lab access. No housing stipend. Free to apply before 16 August 2026; a $20 donation thereafter.

Duration: One month (residency takes place in 2027)

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

The LATITUDE Artist in Residence program (started in 2013) is a one-month production residency where 8-10 artists are granted full access to LATITUDE's facilities and community to develop their practice. Its focus is supporting artists who want to use LATITUDE's printing and scanning services to expand their practice, regardless of medium or experience; past residents include photographers, painters, performance artists, new media artists, and sculptors. WHAT RESIDENTS RECEIVE: a $1,000 printing stipend, unlimited scanning, a personal studio with a calibrated workstation and 24/7 access, training and guidance on tech from staff, an organised public event to present new work, and lifetime free lab access. LATITUDE does not offer a housing stipend but will help schedule studio visits during the month. PUBLIC PROGRAMMING: during the residency each artist puts on one community programming event (past examples include panel discussions, artist talks, performances, workshops, and critiques; a gallery space is available for curation) and is asked to act as a mentor to the community, sharing insights and creative methods. WHO SHOULD APPLY: artists interested in production, education, and tech experimentation; no prior printing experience, art education, or media specificity is required, though professionalism and communication are expected. 2027 PANEL COMMITTEE: Yechen Zhao, B. Ingrid Olson, Teri Carson. TIMELINE: applications open 1 August 2026 (free before 16 August, a $20 donation thereafter) and close 1 September 2026 at 12pm (noon) CST; the selection committee reviews in September, meets to decide finalists in October, and acceptances are sent early November 2026. Apply at latitudechicago.org/artist-in-residence.

item.title: INHABIT #16 and #17: Artist-in-Residence 2027 (Max Planck Institute for Empirical Aesthetics)
item.description:
Organisation: Max Planck Institute for Empirical Aesthetics

Location: Frankfurt am Main, Germany

Award: Artist's fee of EUR 8,000 plus an accommodation fee of EUR 2,000, a production budget depending on the project, and travel costs to and within Frankfurt. Also included: realisation of the final project, collaborations with scientists, access to the institute's library, sound studio and scientific facilities, and curatorial support throughout the residency. No application fee.

Duration: Four months. Two slots: INHABIT #16 runs April to July 2027, INHABIT #17 runs September to December 2027

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

INHABIT is the artist-in-residence programme of the Max Planck Institute for Empirical Aesthetics in Frankfurt am Main, which invites artists from various disciplines to collaborate with its scientists and researchers, treating artistic thinking and knowledge as reflective practices in their own right. The 2027 call is addressed to artists from the performing arts and music, who spend four months creating new work, or developing an existing project, inside a scientific research environment and in dialogue with the institute's researchers. Two slots are open for 2027: INHABIT #16 from April to July 2027 and INHABIT #17 from September to December 2027. Work developed during the residency is presented in cooperation with local arts institutions as an exhibition, performance, concert or other format, complemented by discursive formats. WHO THEY ARE LOOKING FOR: artists from the performing arts and music interested in interdisciplinary collaboration between artistic and scientific fields; artists open to developing and sharing a project as an exhibition, performance, concert or another format; and artists active in contemporary culture who respond to the institute with innovative and challenging ideas. WHAT IS OFFERED: an artist's fee of EUR 8,000, an accommodation fee of EUR 2,000, a project-dependent production budget, travel costs to and in Frankfurt, realisation of the final project, collaborations with scientists, access to the library, sound studio and scientific facilities, and curatorial support during the residency. APPLY through the institute's e-recruiting portal by 1 September 2026, 23:59 CET; the jury decision follows in November 2026. No fee.

item.title: Tartu UNESCO City of Literature Residency for Writers and Translators, Autumn 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Estonian Literary Society (Eesti Kirjanduse Selts), Focal Point for Tartu UNESCO City of Literature

Location: Tartu, Estonia. Open to writers, poets and translators of Estonian literature worldwide.

Award: Monthly stipend of EUR 600 for the two-month stay (EUR 1,200 in total), plus reimbursement of travel costs up to EUR 350. Free accommodation is provided in the Karl Ristikivi residency apartment, which has a bedroom, living room, kitchen, bathroom and exhibition room. One resident is selected. No application fee.

Duration: Two months, 15 October to 15 December 2026, with some flexibility on exact dates

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

The Estonian Literary Society, which coordinates Tartu UNESCO City of Literature, runs an international residency programme for writers and translators that has hosted authors from Slovenia, Ireland, Hungary, the USA, the UK, Ukraine and Canada since 2017. This is the open call for the autumn 2026 slot: one resident stays two months in the Karl Ristikivi residency apartment in Tartu, working on their own writing or translation while connecting with the local literary scene. WHAT THE RESIDENCY OFFERS: a EUR 600 monthly stipend, travel reimbursement up to EUR 350, free accommodation, a local support coordinator to help arrange cultural engagements, and opportunities to perform and present at literary events. The autumn period covers the interdisciplinary literary festival Crazy Tartu on 12 to 14 November, and the resident is offered a slot to perform there alongside writers, poets, musicians and artists from Estonia and abroad. ELIGIBILITY: open to writers, poets and translators of Estonian literature of any nationality; applicants need an upper-intermediate level of spoken English, at least one published book, screenplay, theatre script or translation from Estonian into another language, a demonstrable interest in Estonian culture and literature, a willingness to take part in local literary activities, and a commitment to working on their own literary project during the stay. HOW TO APPLY: complete the online application form linked from the residency page and upload a fragment of up to five pages of a published text (in Estonian or English) or of a published translation. SELECTION: made by a committee representing the Estonian Literary Society, the Estonian Writers Union, the Estonian Literary Museum and the Tartu Literature House Foundation. Results are announced before 15 September 2026. The programme's stated aims are to enhance international exchange, diversify the local literary scene, introduce new foreign authors and their work to Estonian readers, and build lasting connections beyond the residency period. Questions: Marja Unt, eks@kirjandus.ee. Deadline 1 September 2026.

item.title: Le Garage Moderne: OASIS International Artist Residencies 2026 (Bordeaux)
item.description:
Organisation: Le Garage Moderne (European OASIS project)

Location: Bacalan district, Bordeaux, France. Le Garage Moderne is a non-profit car garage and bicycle workshop, a canteen serving sponsored meals, and a cultural venue housing 11 permanent artists, makers and craftswomen, recently returned to its 19th-century building after a two-and-a-half-year renovation.

Award: Five grants. Each artist receives a fee of EUR 1,300 gross (taxes may apply depending on legal status), up to EUR 600 for production expenses such as raw materials, technical services or special tools, a lump-sum travel grant scaled to distance with top-ups for green travel options, a per diem of EUR 45 per day, and accommodation in a self-catering hotel. Access to the shared tools and spaces of Le Garage Moderne is included, subject to the association's regulations. No application fee.

Duration: Two weeks on site. Five overlapping two-week slots, and applicants may choose one or more: 9 to 22 November, 16 to 29 November, 23 November to 6 December, 30 November to 13 December, and 7 to 20 December 2026. Deadline 1 September 2026; pre-selection interviews 15 September; final selection announced 1 October 2026.

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

Second year of Le Garage Moderne's residency cycle within the European OASIS project, offering five grants to international artists for two-week stays in Bordeaux. THE SITE IS THE POINT. Le Garage Moderne is a working non-profit car and bicycle workshop with a neighbourhood canteen and a versatile venue for performing arts, concerts and community gatherings, all at once a productive space, a public space and a community-driven common. Having just moved back into its 19th-century building after a long renovation, the team describes machines and workbenches back in place and a brand-new playground, and invites residents to take over the space and explore its physical and social possibilities. They ask for SITE-SPECIFIC PROPOSALS that play with the verticality, the scale of the space, the community and what they call the hive-like vibe of the venue, where everyone runs around, shouts, gets their hands dirty and learns in the process. DISCIPLINES: any, explicitly including design, visual art, performing arts, film, small-scale architecture, emergency architecture, craft-making, street furniture, sound, and interdisciplinary or community-based practices. Proposals combining artistic creation with the spatial and the social are especially encouraged, and the organisers say plainly that they want to be surprised. WHAT IS EXPECTED: openness to exchange and collaboration with the 11 permanent residents and with 3 local artists recruited through a separate OASIS call; participation in 2 days of masterclass open to members and community, where you describe and share your practice, technique and working context with fellow OASIS residents, local artists, members and staff; and a public outcome, which need not be a large event but must be something the public can experience. RIGHTS: work produced during the residency remains the artist's property, but documentation of it is made by Le Garage Moderne and will be publicised by them for three years after the residency. Note this is a different OASIS partner call from the OASis In the Park (Naples) and Disappearing Landscape (High Tatras) rounds under the same European project.

item.title: University of Johannesburg Artists in Residence 2027
item.description:
Organisation: UJ Arts & Culture, University of Johannesburg

Location: Johannesburg, South Africa. Both physical and remote residencies can be applied for, though office, studio, rehearsal and performance space is limited and not guaranteed.

Award: Stipend of ZAR 12,000 per month across a 10-month residency, so roughly ZAR 120,000 in total. No travel or accommodation budget on top of the stipend, and studio or rehearsal space is limited rather than guaranteed. No application fee.

Duration: 10 months during 2027

Deadline: Closed 31 Aug 2026

UJ Arts & Culture's annual residency gives artists a monthly stipend and an institutional base at the University of Johannesburg for ten months, with the option of a remote rather than physical residency. Disciplines covered are visual and fine arts, music, theatre, performance and dance, design, film and television, and literary arts. A virtual information session with Pieter Jacobs, Head of UJ Arts & Culture, was scheduled for 17 August 2026 to walk applicants through the process. ELIGIBILITY: applicants must hold a relevant post-school qualification, with preference for master's and PhD holders, and must not be affiliated with another tertiary institution in South Africa. Preference has historically gone to artists with African connections. APPLICATION: via the online form linked from the UJ Arts & Culture residency page; contact kmachoga@uj.ac.za or +27 11 559 1476 with questions. DEADLINE: 31 August 2026. No fee.

item.title: Delfina Foundation: Open Call for Curators Based in Central and West Africa (London residency)
item.description:
Organisation: Delfina Foundation

Location: Delfina Foundation, 29-31 Catherine Place, London, UK. Applicants must hold nationality and be based in an eligible Central or West African country.

Award: Fully supported: a return economy-class flight, airport transfers in the UK, reimbursement of visa fees if required, a living allowance of GBP 40 per day, a materials and research allowance of GBP 70 per week, a travel pass for London's public transport network, and a single bedroom with a desk at Delfina Foundation, a house hosting up to eight residents with shared bathrooms, laundry rooms, kitchen, library and dining room. Supported by Delfina Foundation's Network of Patrons for Africa. No application fee.

Duration: Six or twelve weeks within Delfina's winter 2027 season, which runs 5 January to 28 March 2027.

Deadline: Closed 30 Aug 2026

With support from Delfina Foundation's Network of Patrons for Africa, Delfina is offering a six- or twelve-week London residency within its winter 2027 season to curators based in Central and West Africa. ELIGIBILITY: applicants must hold nationality and be based in one of Angola, Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cabo Verde, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Cote d'Ivoire, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Republic of the Congo, Sao Tome and Principe, Senegal, Sierra Leone, The Gambia or Togo; and must have at least five years of professional curatorial practice in a freelance, academic or institutional context. THE PROGRAMME: alongside time and space to develop their work, residents get guided visits to museums, galleries, non-profits, artist-run spaces and studios, plus trips to institutions outside London; opportunities to meet and engage with artists, curators, academics and researchers through organised presentations, studio visits, events and meals; professional development including presentations and crits, portfolio reviews and mentoring activities to strengthen their practice; and collaborative exchange between residents through informal gatherings and meals. APPLY via the application form on the open call page; Delfina strongly recommends reading the Guidance Notes document carefully before starting. Deadline Sunday 30 August 2026, 23:59 BST.

item.title: Archipel Butor Livre de dialogue Creation Residency 2027
item.description:
Organisation: Archipel Butor

Location: Lucinges (74380), Haute-Savoie, France, in the house of the writer Michel Butor.

Award: Creation grant of EUR 2,000 gross per month per artist, so roughly EUR 4,000 each across the two months and EUR 8,000 for the pair. Up to two return journeys per person are covered within France and Europe. Accommodation is provided in Michel Butor's writer's house. No application fee.

Duration: Two months in total, taken as eight weeks that may be split, starting from January 2027. Time is split 70 percent creation and 30 percent mediation activities.

Deadline: Closed 30 Aug 2026

Archipel Butor runs its creation residency out of the former home of the writer Michel Butor in Lucinges, Haute-Savoie, and this call is for a livre de dialogue, a dialogue book made jointly by a writer and a visual artist. The residency exists to give a pair concentrated time to develop a book together and to raise the profile of artist book culture and of collaboration at the centre of artistic process. WHO APPLIES: a pair made up of an author with a project for a dialogue book and a visual artist collaborating on it. The two do not need to have worked together before, but both must be present during the shared periods. WHAT IS PROVIDED: EUR 2,000 gross per month per artist, up to two return trips per person within France and Europe, and accommodation in the writer's house. STRUCTURE: two months in total, taken as eight weeks which may be split across the year from January 2027, with 70 percent of the time given to creation and 30 percent to mediation and public engagement activities. A videoconference is held with the selected laureates beforehand to arrange on-site scheduling and the mediation sessions. HOW TO APPLY: follow the official call document downloadable from the residency page, submitting a single PDF to accueil@archipel-butor.fr containing a joint letter, biographies of both practitioners, the artistic proposal, technical specifications and the proposed mediation activities. NOTE: the call and application file are in French. Deadline 30 August 2026.

item.title: Collar Works: Elizabeth Murray Artist Residency (EMAR) 2027
item.description:
Organisation: Collar Works

Location: In person on a 77-acre farm in Granville, Washington County, New York, USA (the former summer home of Elizabeth Murray and Bob Holman). Collar Works itself is based in Troy, New York.

Award: Fully supported: there is no cost to participate for accepted artists. Private bedroom accommodation with shared bathrooms in the farmhouse, 24-hour access to a semi-private studio in the barn that housed Elizabeth Murray's studio, all food provided (dinner cooked and eaten communally), and use of the property including a swimming pool, pond and 77 acres of fields and woods. Accepted artists also receive a USD 500 stipend to use at their discretion towards travel, materials or other associated costs. The Family Residency additionally provides free full-day (9am to 3pm) childcare as a parallel creative residency for children aged 5 to 12, plus a dedicated Kids Art Studio. APPLICATION FEE: USD 35 (the first month of the application period was free; the fee applies from 1 August 2026).

Duration: Two weeks for individual artists, one week for families. 2027 individual sessions: Session 1, 15 to 29 May 2027; Session 2, 1 to 15 June 2027. 2027 family session: Session 3, 19 to 26 June 2027. Finalist interviews November 2026; final notification December 2026.

Deadline: 01 Oct 2026

The Elizabeth Murray Artist Residency gives emerging, underrepresented and established artists an immersive, communal atmosphere for art-making and dialogue on a 77-acre farm in Granville, New York, the classic farmhouse where the late Elizabeth Murray spent more than two decades of summers and kept her studio in the large, cathedral-like dairy barn. Murray, who died in 2007, won a Skowhegan Medal in Painting in 1986, a MacArthur grant in 1999 and a MoMA career retrospective in 2005; her husband Bob Holman is a poet and arts activist who founded the Bowery Poetry Club. In 2017 the Murray-Holman family partnered with Collar Works, a nonprofit contemporary arts organisation in Troy, New York, to build a summer residency carrying the legacy forward. EMAR is explicitly designed around the critical needs of emerging and underrepresented artists and of artists with children, with an active commitment to diversity, equity, accessibility and inclusion, and describes itself as a safe space for creative risk-taking, personal growth and respite. Work is primarily in visual and literary arts, though the programme supports new contemporary work across many art forms. TWO TRACKS: the INDIVIDUAL RESIDENCY takes up to five artists per session (including onsite artist-staff) for two weeks, with 24-hour access to semi-private studios in the barn, a private bedroom in the farmhouse, shared bathrooms, communal living room, kitchen and a library holding Elizabeth Murray's personal art book collection. The FAMILY RESIDENCY invites three to four artists and their families for one week, with a private bedroom (families may need to room together), a semi-private studio in the same barn, and full-day childcare running as a parallel creative residency for children aged 5 to 12, focused on art and nature programming: while parent artists get uninterrupted studio time, children work in their own EMAR Kids Art Studio, explore outside through guided activities, play, swim, read and take guided field trips to local farms and museums. Partners are welcome to join and help with childcare, but the programme is committed to fully supporting artists who want or need to attend solo with their children, and Collar Works works case by case with each artist to put the necessary support and equipment in place before arrival given the rural setting. APPLICATION requires artist information, a statement of intent (250 to 500 words), an artist biography (250 words), ten examples of recent work (visual arts as JPEGs up to 2MB each, with a PDF of links or a curated URL page for video and media works including any passwords; literary arts as up to three poems totalling max six pages, or max ten pages of prose) and a list of works with title, medium, date and size. Applications go through Submittable and close 1 October 2026 (the Submittable listing shows a 2 October 2026 06:00 close in its own timezone). Questions and technical assistance: info@collarworks.org.

item.title: Scuola Piccola Zattere: International Fellowship and Residency 2027 (Venice)
item.description:
Organisation: Scuola Piccola Zattere

Location: Venice, Italy. Open to any nationality.

Award: EUR 5,000 fellowship grant plus a EUR 2,000 research budget, accommodation in Venice, an individual study space within a shared studio, and round-trip travel to Venice. Collectives and duos share a single grant and one accommodation. No application fee.

Duration: Three months, in one of two slots: early January to early April 2027, or mid-April to mid-July 2027. Applicants may name one slot or indicate availability for both.

Deadline: 04 Sep 2026

Scuola Piccola Zattere is an independent non-profit centre for continuous education and research in the expanded field of contemporary arts, running exhibitions, commissions, fellowships, workshops, seminars, performances and public discussions as one connected research ecosystem rather than separate strands. Two international fellowships are offered. The support is unusually solid for a research fellowship: EUR 5,000 as a grant, EUR 2,000 as a research budget, accommodation, travel and a study space for three months. SEASON THEME: the 2026-2027 cycle is titled Living Document, investigating archives, regulatory documents, collective rituals, games, performative instructions, and the relationship between bodies, architecture and social organisation. Fellows join that shared inquiry while continuing their own work, and are expected to keep an active presence in the institution and contribute to public events through workshops, seminars, presentations, screenings or performances. The fellowship overlaps with the run-up to and opening of the 2027 Architecture Biennale, which is a real advantage if your research benefits from that traffic. ELIGIBILITY: artists, curators, researchers, architects, choreographers, performers and writers of any nationality, as individuals, collectives or duos. Good English is required, and non-EU applicants need a valid passport for international travel. No age limit, but the organisers say it is especially intended for practitioners in the post-academic stage of their career, typically under 40. You must be prepared to spend the full period in Venice, so this is not a remote or partial-attendance fellowship. WHAT THEY WANT: an active research process that can develop through discussion and experimentation, tied to the Living Document theme, not a finished stand-alone project proposal. The motivation letter, portfolio and public programming proposal are read as one integrated application. Deadline 4 September 2026 at 10:00 CEST.

item.title: DRIFT: Choreographer Open Call 2026-27 (Dance and Research In The Future Time)
item.description:
Organisation: DRIFT, a four-year Creative Europe cooperation of ten organisations led by Theatre de Liege and Maison de la danse

Location: Activities across Europe: kick-off in Berlin, Festival Lab in Tunis, showcase in Lyon, online labs, plus a residency hosted by your own national DRIFT partner. Applicants must be based in Belgium, France, Germany (Berlin region only), Greece, Norway, Italy, Spain, Ukraine, Tunisia or Portugal, and apply through the partner organisation for their country of residence.

Award: EUR 20,000 research budget per choreographer, covering artistic fees, travel, accommodation and optional collaborator costs. Also included: an Onboarding Lab, two weeks of residency with your national DRIFT partner, three collaborative Online Labs, a Festival Lab in Tunis, individual artistic mentoring and individual curatorial mentoring, and a work-in-progress presentation at the Biennale de la danse in Lyon. No application fee.

Duration: November 2026 to September 2027. Kick-off in Berlin 30 November to 1 December 2026; Festival Lab in Tunis 18-21 March 2027; Biennale de la danse showcase in Lyon 18-25 September 2027.

Deadline: Closed 31 Aug 2026

DRIFT (Dance and Research In The Future Time) is a four-year Creative Europe cooperation between ten European organisations, led by Theatre de Liege and Maison de la danse. The distinguishing feature is that it funds artistic research rather than production: you are expected to arrive with questions, not a finished piece you already intend to make, and reviewers read every section of the application through that lens. STRUCTURE: each of the ten partner organisations selects one choreographer from its own country, forming a cohort of ten. Over the programme you get an Onboarding Lab, two weeks of residency with your national partner, three collaborative Online Labs, a Festival Lab in Tunis, individual artistic and curatorial mentoring, and a work-in-progress showcase at the Biennale de la danse in Lyon, all backed by a EUR 20,000 research budget that covers your fees, travel, accommodation and any collaborators. SECOND PHASE: after a further evaluation, five of the ten artists may receive co-production support and touring across the DRIFT network. That phase is separate from this application and is not guaranteed. ELIGIBILITY: professional choreographers in contemporary dance or performance, at a mid-career stage, meaning an established national practice but not yet fully established internationally. You must be based in Belgium, France, Germany (Berlin region only), Greece, Norway, Italy, Spain, Ukraine, Tunisia or Portugal, and you apply through the partner organisation representing your country of residence, not centrally. Good English and availability for all programme dates are required. The country list is strict, so check it before you start. TIMELINE: applications opened 1 July 2026 and close 31 August 2026; selection through September; results 9 October 2026; programme runs November 2026 to September 2027.

item.title: Residing Non-linear Technologies and Sonic Worldings (M-Cult x Titanik, Helsinki and Turku)
item.description:
Organisation: Art and Media Culture Agency M-Cult (Helsinki) and Arte artists' association / Titanik gallery (Turku)

Location: Finland; one month in Helsinki and one month in Turku. Open to artists from or based in Nordic and Baltic countries.

Award: EUR 3,500 artist fee plus EUR 2,000 production budget, two months' accommodation split between Helsinki and Turku, and one return travel ticket from a Nordic-Baltic country. No application fee stated.

Duration: Two months, February to March 2027 (one month in each city)

Deadline: Closed 30 Aug 2026

A new pilot residency from Art and Media Culture Agency M-Cult in Helsinki and Arte artists' association / Titanik gallery in Turku, sitting at the intersection of art, media and sonic practice, funded by the Nordic-Baltic Mobility Programme for Culture from Nordic Culture Point. TWO ARTISTS will be selected. THE PREMISE: the programme treats technology as a situated practice and deliberately shifts attention away from the progress narratives promoted by large global technology companies, toward local, indigenous and community-oriented perspectives. It focuses on making vernacular and non-linear technological and sonic environments visible, foregrounding vibrant local histories and traditions across the Nordic and Baltic region, and asks what non-linear sonic and media practice might look like in the current social, political and cultural landscape. WHAT EACH ARTIST RECEIVES: EUR 3,500 artist fee; EUR 2,000 production budget; accommodation for two months divided between Helsinki and Turku, one month in each; travel costs for one return ticket from a Nordic-Baltic country; access to Titanik's residency studio space and a working desk at M-Cult's office during each stay; mentoring and curatorial support from both organisations' staff; and networking into the Finnish media art and contemporary art scenes. In return the artist develops in-depth or focused research and presents their practice and research at two public events, one in each city. The Good Life Residents Program is a six-month Roosevelt Institute initiative that develops new leaders and elevates bold ideas across six economic policy priorities under its Good Life Agenda. Each topic area hosts a cohort of 3 to 4 residents plus 1 to 2 senior Topic Advisors (academics, policy leaders, organizers or government practitioners) who provide strategic and intellectual mentorship and moderate the closing event. Framing: breakneck investment in generative AI technology and infrastructure is distorting the stock market, profit measures, bond issuance, the pace and composition of growth, job creation and trade policy, with seven tech companies accounting for more than a third of S&P 500 market capitalisation and complex, sometimes circular financial arrangements obscuring risk. Suggested lines of inquiry include what government interventions could improve public oversight, risk allocation and direction-setting in private markets; how other investments could be coordinated and scaled if AI spending is crowding them out; what role public spending or new institutions could play in catalysing technology R&D designed to support workers, sustainability and supply chains; what democratic input mechanisms would keep state influence over capital flows less vulnerable to corruption; and how federal AI policy should address public hostility to data centre investments alongside national security and competitiveness.
